mainEntity.name: How much does a Suzuki S-Cross SX4 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement Suzuki S-Cross SX4 engine typically costs between £1,500 and £3,800 for a rebuilt unit fitted by a specialist, depending on whether you have the M16A petrol or D16AA diesel. Used engines start from around £350 supply-only.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Suzuki S-Cross SX4 M16A?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start-up, which may persist as the engine warms up.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Suzuki S-Cross SX4?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2013-2019 Suzuki S-Cross SX4 typically retains significant value (£5,000-£14,000 depending on condition and mileage), so a rebuilt engine at £1,500-£3,800 fitted is usually a sound investment. For earlier (2006-2013) models valued under £3,000, consider a good used engine instead.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Suzuki S-Cross SX4 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full engine replacement typically takes 2-5 days depending on the workshop's schedule and parts availability.

mainEntity.name: Will a Peugeot/Citroën 1.9 DDIS engine fit my Suzuki S-Cross SX4?

acceptedAnswer.text: The D19AA engine in the Suzuki S-Cross SX4 is a PSA-derived engine shared with Peugeot 307, Citroën C4, and MINI models. However, direct compatibility is not guaranteed due to differences in engine management, wiring, and mounting points.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the SX4 and S-Cross SX4 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The SX4 (2006-2013) uses the M16A petrol and D19AA diesel. The S-Cross SX4 (2013-present) uses the M16A petrol and D16AA diesel.

historyTimeline.h2: Suzuki S-Cross SX4 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Suzuki SX4 arrived in 2006 as a compact crossover, with the S-Cross badge introduced for the second generation from 2013. The range has been powered by a mix of petrol and diesel engines across two generations, with the 1.6-litre M16A petrol and the 1.9/1.6 DDIS diesels dominating UK sales.

milestones.description: Suzuki SX4 launched with M16A 1.6-litre VVT petrol (107-120hp) as the primary engine
D19AA 1.9 DDIS diesel introduced (120hp, PSA-based 8V turbo)
Minor facelift; M16A power output increased to 120hp
D19AA diesel production ends; replaced by D16AA 1.6 DDIS (120hp, 16V) with the S-Cross generation
Suzuki SX4 S-Cross launched with M16A petrol and D16AA diesel; ALLGRIP 4WD available
2016 - S-Cross continues with minor specification updates; SZ-T and SZ5 trim levels
Facelift with revised grille and lighting; D16AA diesel continues
Final year of D16AA diesel production
Suzuki S-Cross petrol-only from this point; 1.4 Boosterjet replaces M16A

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Suzuki S-Cross SX4 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Suzuki S-Cross SX4 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Suzuki S-Cross SX4 has served UK drivers reliably across two generations, but engine issues do arise with age and mileage. The M16A petrol is prone to timing chain stretch, while the D19AA diesel suffers from injector and turbo failures. The later D16AA diesel is more robust but DPF issues are common. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the Suzuki S-Cross SX4 M16A Develops Rattling
problems.rootCause: The M16A uses a timing chain that can stretch over time. A rattling noise on cold start-up is the classic warning sign, caused by a worn tensioner or chain stretch allowing the chain to slap against the guide.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioner and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early with rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt M16A with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has failed and engine is damaged, or high-mileage engine with multiple issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2006-2013 Suzuki S-Cross SX4 1.6 is valued between £1,500 and £6,000 depending on condition and mileage [THIRD-PARTY - Parkers/Auto Trader market observation]. For 2013-2019 S-Cross models, values range from £5,000 to £14,000. On earlier models with sub-£3,000 value, a used engine may be more cost-effective. For later S-Cross models, a rebuilt engine is usually justified.
problems.recommendation: If you hear rattling from your Suzuki S-Cross SX4 M16A on start-up, have the timing chain inspected immediately. Catching it early could save you thousands. If the engine has already failed, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components is the best long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M16A Suzuki S-Cross SX4 engine prices

problems.h4: Injector and Turbo Failure - The D19AA DDIS Diesel Weak Points
problems.rootCause: The D19AA is a PSA-sourced 1.9-litre diesel engine. Injector failure (seal leaks, electrical faults) is the most common issue. Turbocharger failure, EGR valve clogging, and crankshaft pulley failure are also well-documented.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of faulty injector and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early; prevents further engine damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of turbocharger unit and oil supply lines
repairOptions.longevity: When turbo has failed or is causing performance issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt D19AA with upgraded components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When multiple components have failed or engine is high-mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A 2006-2010 Suzuki S-Cross SX4 D19AA is typically valued between £1,500 and £5,000. With replacement cost often exceeding vehicle value on sub-£3,000 examples, consider scrap value before committing to a full rebuild. A used engine may be the more economical choice.
problems.recommendation: The D19AA is a known-cost engine. If multiple injectors have failed or the turbo is also showing signs of wear, a full replacement with a rebuilt engine often makes more sense than repeated individual repairs. For lower-value vehicles, a good used engine may be the most cost-effective option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt D19AA Suzuki S-Cross SX4 engine prices

problems.h4: DPF Regeneration Faults - The D16AA DDIS Diesel's Urban Weakness
problems.rootCause: The D16AA 1.6-litre diesel is fitted with a DPF that can clog with soot if the car is used primarily for short urban journeys, preventing successful regeneration. This can lead to warning lights and limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Specialist tool forced regeneration of DPF
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early; requires motorway driving to complete

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of DPF or professional cleaning
repairOptions.longevity: When forced regeneration fails or DPF is blocked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt D16AA with cleaned/replaced DPF, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When DPF failure has caused engine damage or engine has other issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A 2013-2019 Suzuki S-Cross SX4 D16AA is typically valued between £5,000 and £14,000. With replacement cost under £4,000 fitted through a specialist, replacement is usually justified for most examples.
problems.recommendation: The D16AA is generally a robust engine, but DPF issues are common on urban-used cars. Regular motorway driving and the correct oil spec are essential for longevity. If the DPF has failed and the engine is otherwise healthy, replacing the DPF may be sufficient. However, if the engine shows other signs of wear, a rebuilt unit may be the better long-term investment.
